'''Alejandro Sánchez Alvarado''' is a Venezuelan-American [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]]. He is an Emeritus Investigator of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]], and President and Chief Scientific Officer of the [[Stowers Institute for Medical Research]]. The Sánchez Alvarado Laboratory focuses on understanding the regenerative capabilities of the [[planarian]] [[flatworm]] ''[[Schmidtea mediterranea]].''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mbl.edu/research/mbl-fellows/alejandro-sanchez-alvarado/|title=Alejandro Sánchez Alvarado|website=www.mbl.edu|access-date=2016-11-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://planaria.stowers.org/regeneration.php|title=Regeneration|website=planaria.stowers.org|access-date=2016-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107055324/http://planaria.stowers.org/regeneration.php|archive-date=2016-11-07|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.stowers.org/faculty/s%C3%A1nchez-lab|title=Sánchez Lab {{!}} Stowers Institute for Medical Research|website=www.stowers.org|access-date=2016-11-12}}</ref>  In 2015, Sánchez Alvarado was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2018 for his distinguished and continuing achievements in original scientific research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stowers.org/media/news/apr-22-2015|title=Stowers Investigator elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences {{!}} Stowers Institute for == Life ==
Born in [[Venezuela]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://thenode.biologists.com/an-interview-with-alejandro-sanchez-alvarado/interview/|title=An interview with Alejandro Sánchez Alvarado - the Node|date=2013-09-11|newspaper=the Node|language=en-US|access-date=2016-11-12}}</ref> Sánchez Alvarado attended the Colegio Emil Friedman for elementary and high school education, where he first cultivated his interest in [[biology]]. After receiving a BS in molecular biology and [[chemistry]] from [[Vanderbilt University]] in 1986, he attended the [[University of Cincinnati Academic Health Center|University of Cincinnati College of Medicine]] for his PhD in [[pharmacology]] and [[cell biophysics]] in the laboratory of Dr. Jeffrey Robbins. After receiving his Ph.D. in 1992, he carried out postdoctoral studies from 1994 to 1995 in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]] at the [[Carnegie Institution of Washington]], Department of Embryology under the mentorship of Dr. [[Donald D. Brown]]. He was then appointed Staff Associate at the Department of Embryology to run his own independent research group and during which he started to develop the planarian ''[[S. mediterranea]]'' as a research organism to study animal regeneration <ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
